species.real: In the 1960s the pesticide DDT left peregrines laying eggs so thin they broke under the sitting bird, and the British population crashed until the chemicals were banned.
species.name: Peregrin

dex.text: Looks down on the city from the top of a tower and considers everyone below a bit slow. Dressed in sharp slate grey and moves like a stone that has been thrown.
dex.fact: The peregrine is the fastest animal on Earth in a dive, reaching over 300 km/h.

species.real: During the Second World War peregrines were shot in Britain on government orders, to stop them eating the carrier pigeons that brought messages home.
species.name: Stoopfalcon

dex.text: Has a quiet word with the pigeons, then drops out of the sky to check they were listening. Nests on ledges high above the traffic, which suits it very well.
dex.fact: Peregrines nest on cliffs and tall buildings, and cathedrals and city towers have become favourite ledges.
